messages:
Customer Ops: Heads up — AcmeCorp reported a spike of 503s + client timeouts hitting our hosted inference API in eu-west-1 starting ~09:12 UTC. They say it happens during their nightly batch window when they send ~300 concurrent streaming requests. They included an SDK loop log and some curl traces.

Support: Can you paste the first error snippet? Need to know if it's 502/503/504 and whether streaming chunks failed or connection reset. Also passing ticket #INC-4721 to eng-sre.

Customer Ops: From the customer logs: 
```
2026-03-07T09:12:05Z - request_id=abc123 - status=503 - message="upstream unavailable"
2026-03-07T09:12:05Z - sdk_retry - attempt=1
2026-03-07T09:12:12Z - status=504 - timeout waiting for backend
```
They also included curl where a single long request returns 503 immediately: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -d '{"input":"...long prompt..."}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

SRE Oncall: Thanks. Initial hypothesis: gateway capacity/backpressure in eu-west-1 under bursty streaming workload. Asking eng-runtime to check ingress QPS, per-proxy queue depth, and recent deploys. @eng-runtime can you check the gateway error rate + 5xx breakdown for that region in the 09:00-09:20 window?

eng-runtime: Looking now. Quick telemetry: between 09:10-09:15 we see a sharp rise in 5xx for model-route `gpt-large-serve` in eu-west-1. Errors are mostly 503 and `upstream_unavailable`. No config deploys in that minute, but we had a scheduled nightly batch job moving a few hosts to maintenance at 09:05 that may have reduced capacity temporarily.

eng-runtime: Dumping relevant query counts: 
```
route=gpt-large-serve region=eu-west-1 window=09:00-09:20
requests_total=18k
5xx_total=1.1k
503=980
504=90
```
Queue latency percentiles spiked (p95->p99) and we saw continuous batching timeouts.

SRE Oncall: Sounds like capacity dip + burst = gateway couldn't route fast enough and returned 503s. Customer SDK retried aggressively which caused retry storm and drove more pressure. Need to coordinate protective measures.

support: Customer is asking for immediate mitigation and a rollback-free ETA. They want either a region fallback or temporary capacity bump. What are options?

eng-runtime: Short-term options: 1) increase autoscaling target in eu-west-1 (can be done, ~15-20min to add capacity), 2) enable temporary geo-fallback to us-west for that customer (requires config change and will add latency), 3) patch gateway to return 429 instead of 503 for overloaded queues (safer for clients with backoff).

devex: Note — customer SDK currently treats 503 as transient and retries with no jitter. We should recommend immediate client patch: exponential backoff + jitter and a max retry cap for streaming. Sending a recommended SDK snippet: 
```
// pseudo-SDK: add jittered exponential backoff
await client.generate(req, { retries: 3, backoff: (i) => Math.pow(2,i)*100 + Math.random()*200 });
```

Customer Ops: AcmeCorp prefers us to handle routing/fallback on our side if possible. They're worried about cross-region data residency but said for the night window they can accept fallback to us-west temporarily.

SRE Oncall: I'm going to kick off an immediate autoscaling bump for eu-west (increasing reserved pool by +30%) and also open a geo-fallback rule for AcmeCorp to route to us-west on 503 for the next 2 hours. I'll monitor error rate.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: scale-up eu-west reserved-pool +30% (task id: scale-789). ETA ~14m.

eng-runtime: Also creating a short-lived rate limiter per-customer on the gateway to smooth retry storms. Rule: token-bucket 120 req/min per-customer with burst 40. This will convert sudden spikes into 429s.

support: Please confirm when autoscale completes so we can update the customer. Also: should we send a pre-baked mitigation note? Something like: "We've increased capacity and enabled temporary geo-fallback; please apply SDK backoff to avoid retry amplification."

eng-runtime: Scale completed at 09:26 UTC. 5xx rate dropped to baseline within ~4 minutes. Route fallback enabled at 09:28. Observed customer traffic routed -> us-west for ~12 minutes. Post-mitigation metrics: 5xx reduced from 6% -> 0.3% for the window.

SRE Oncall: Closing loop: primary root cause = capacity dip due to maintenance + bursty streaming workload + aggressive client retries. Actions: 
- reverted maintenance stagger to avoid future overlap with customer batch windows (ops runbook updated)
- enabled soft per-customer limiting on gateway (temporary; will refine)
- recommend SDK backoff change (coord with devex)
- add automated anomaly alert for p95 queue latency + sudden 5xx bump per-region

devex: I'll draft an SDK advisory and sample code for exponential backoff + retry budget. Suggest tagging it into the customer support reply.

support: Messaging to customer drafted. Sending now: "We identified a transient capacity reduction in eu-west-1 during your batch window that coincided with aggressive client retries. We increased capacity and enabled a temporary geo-fallback to us-west; 5xx rates have returned to normal. To avoid amplification, please upgrade to our SDK patch which includes jittered exponential backoff. Let us know if you want us to keep geo-fallback active longer while you roll changes." :thumbsup:

Customer Ops: Customer replied: "Thanks — errors stopped after your intervention. We'll patch SDK tomorrow. Please keep geo-fallback off after midnight."

SRE Oncall: Marking incident resolved and filing post-incident notes. Will create follow-up tasks for: improve gateway overload responses (429 vs 503), implement smarter routing fallback automation, and update autoscaler to respect maintenance windows.

support: Closing ticket INC-4721. If anything else pops up, reopen thread. :eyes:
